lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata, don't walk yet. I wrote down everything that happened since you left. Number one. Boppy saw the Big One again.
lines.script: [bossy, small teacher] Tata, don't walk yet. [proud] I wrote down EVERYTHING that happened since you left. [reading aloud] Number one. Boppy saw the Big One again.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: It's bigger than a BUS! It ate a boat!
lines.script: [shouting, delighted] It's bigger than a BUS! [certain, stating a fact] It ate a boat!

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: It did not eat a boat. Nobody's ever seen it but Boppy, and he's been saying it for twenty years.
lines.script: [flat, correcting] It did NOT eat a boat. [matter of fact] Nobody's ever seen it but Boppy, and he's been saying it for twenty years.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Twenty years, one witness. That's a strong number one. What's number two?
lines.script: [serious, taking notes in his head] Twenty years, one witness. [sincere, impressed] That's a STRONG number one. [eager] What's number two?

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Number two. Deedee made apple muffins. They're for you, so nobody's allowed to have one yet.
lines.script: [reading aloud] Number two. Deedee made apple muffins. [strict] They're for you, so nobody's allowed to have one yet.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I licked one. Only the top!
lines.script: [cheerful confession] I licked one. [quick, reassuring] Only the TOP!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Thank you for telling me, Rose. That one's yours. Grace, I'm so sorry. Number two can't wait.
lines.script: [warm, formal] Thank you for telling me, Rose. That one's yours. [truly apologetic] Grace, I'm so sorry. [urgent] Number two can't WAIT.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Number three. Rose licked a muffin.
lines.script: [flat, writing as she talks] [punchline] Number three. Rose licked a muffin.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Brother! I'm watching you from the window. I've seen people walk faster in ski boots.
lines.script: [loud, teasing, Long Island] Brother! I'm watching you from the window. [punchline, cheerful] I've seen people walk faster in SKI boots.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I'm carrying a child and receiving a news report.
lines.script: [dignified, defending himself] I'm carrying a child and receiving a NEWS report.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: I carried both of them up that street with the groceries. Go hug Mom. I'm coming over after my run.
lines.script: [bragging, fast] I carried BOTH of them up that street with the groceries. [warm, bossy] Go hug Mom. I'm coming over after my run.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Your mother says I'm slow.
lines.script: [mock wounded] Your mother says I'm slow.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: You are slow. I've been on number four since the mailbox.
lines.script: [flat, sassy] You ARE slow. [punchline, level] I've been on number four since the mailbox.

lines.speaker: Aunt Ellie
lines.text: Tom. They gave you a seat that turns into a bed, and you still got off that plane wrinkled.
lines.script: [cool, elegant, Long Island] Tom. [measured, faintly disappointed] They gave you a seat that turns into a BED, [punchline, level] and you still got off that plane wrinkled.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Hi, Aunt Ellie. It's a travel wrinkle. It's supposed to fall out by dinner.
lines.script: [warm, a little defensive] Hi, Aunt Ellie. [earnest, explaining] It's a TRAVEL wrinkle. It's supposed to fall out by dinner.

lines.speaker: Aunt Ellie
lines.text: Then I'll look at you again at dinner. Come in. Rose, darling, what is that on your hands?
lines.script: [dry, unhurried] Then I'll look at you again at dinner. [gracious] Come in. [crisp, kind] Rose, darling, what is that on your HANDS?

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Cinnamon! From Deedee's muffin!
lines.script: [proud, loud] Cinnamon! From Deedee's MUFFIN!

lines.speaker: Aunt Ellie
lines.text: Then you'll stay up there, please. Your uncle wipes clean. My chairs don't.
lines.script: [calm, certain] Then you'll stay up there, please. [punchline, cool] Your uncle wipes clean. My CHAIRS don't.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Aunt Ellie, I'm reading Tata everything he missed. You're number four.
lines.script: [bossy, reporting] Aunt Ellie, I'm reading Tata everything he missed. [important] You're number FOUR.

lines.speaker: Aunt Ellie
lines.text: Am I? What did I do?
lines.script: [one raised eyebrow] Am I? [mild interest] What did I do?

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: You got new curtains.
lines.script: [plain, reading] You got new curtains.

lines.speaker: Aunt Ellie
lines.text: I did. And what's number three?
lines.script: [level] I did. [careful] And what's number THREE?

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Rose licked a muffin.
lines.script: [flat] Rose licked a muffin.

lines.speaker: Aunt Ellie
lines.text: Then the curtains are three, Grace. Fix your list. I'm not coming in behind a licked muffin.
lines.script: [crisp, final] Then the curtains are three, Grace. Fix your list. [punchline, composed] I'm not coming in behind a LICKED muffin.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Aunt Ellie, did you miss Tata?
lines.script: [loud, curious] Aunt Ellie, did you MISS Tata?

lines.speaker: Aunt Ellie
lines.text: Fine. The street was quieter without him, and I didn't care for it. Now go and see your mother, Tom, before I change my mind.
lines.script: [clipped, reluctant] Fine. [plain, quick] The street was quieter without him, and I didn't CARE for it. [brisk, businesslike] Now go and see your mother, Tom, before I change my mind.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: There he is! Come here. Let me look at you. I missed that face. Now sit, you're having a muffin.
lines.script: [bright, thrilled, Long Island] There he is! Come here. Let me look at you. [warm, plain] I missed that FACE. [firm] Now sit, you're having a muffin.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Hi, Mom. I missed yours too. Is that the cinnamon topping? I've been thinking about that topping since we flew over Kansas.
lines.script: [warm] Hi, Mom. I missed yours too. [sniffing, hopeful] Is that the cinnamon topping? [earnest confession] I've been thinking about that topping since we flew over KANSAS.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Twelve of them, and all twelve are still there. I've been standing between that pan and your father since six this morning.
lines.script: [proud] Twelve of them, and all twelve are still there. [dry, pointed] I've been standing between that pan and your FATHER since six this morning.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: In my own kitchen! Tom, back at Rikers I had a key to every door in the place, and here I can't get near a muffin. You know, one time a fella tried to walk out of the mess hall with a whole loaf of bread under his hat...
lines.script: [goofy outrage] In my own KITCHEN! [chatty, building] Tom, back at Rikers I had a key to every door in the place, and here I can't get near a MUFFIN. [settling into a story, relaxed] You know, one time a fella tried to walk out of the mess hall with a whole loaf of bread under his hat...

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: AHHH! DEEDEE!
lines.script: [real scream] AHHH! DEEDEE!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: GAH! I'm on the floor. Grace, is that your elbow or mine?
lines.script: [real yelp] GAH! [breathless, amazed] I'm on the floor. [polite, laughing at himself] Grace, is that your elbow or mine?

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: It's mine! Tata, get UP, it's getting away!
lines.script: [scared kid] It's MINE! [taking charge, urgent] Tata, get UP, it's getting away!

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: That thing took my good twelve-cup pan! I don't even put that pan in the DISHWASHER.
lines.script: [shocked, loud] That thing took my good twelve-cup PAN! [low, indignant] I don't even put that pan in the DISHWASHER.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: ...and I only caught him because the hat kept getting taller. Where'd the muffins go?
lines.script: [finishing his story, pleased, has noticed nothing] ...and I only caught him because the hat kept getting TALLER. [mild, puzzled] Where'd the muffins go?

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: A ball of mud came through the door and took them. Pan and all.
lines.script: [brisk, matter of fact] A ball of mud came through the door and took them. Pan and all.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: The mud gets a muffin and I don't?
lines.script: [hurt, baffled] [punchline] The MUD gets a muffin and I don't?

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Girls, sneakers. Tom, hold the door. Hubby, you stay right there. When we get them back, the first one's yours.
lines.script: [charge nurse, fast] Girls, sneakers. Tom, hold the door. Hubby, you stay right there. [softer, a promise] When we get them back, the first one's yours.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: The first one. Tom, you heard her.
lines.script: [satisfied, pointing] The FIRST one. Tom, you heard her.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Hello, mud! Can we please have Deedee's muffins back? Thank you!
lines.script: [loud, friendly, very polite] Hello, mud! Can we PLEASE have Deedee's muffins back? Thank you!

lines.speaker: Mudling
lines.text: No. Ours now.
lines.script: [thick, wet, flat] No. Ours now.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: But I said PLEASE!
lines.script: [outraged, disbelieving] But I said PLEASE!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: She did. I was right here. It was an excellent please.
lines.script: [formal, indignant for her] She did. I was right here. [punchline, certain] It was an EXCELLENT please.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Girls, behind me. You three have till I count to three. Then I'm getting the hose.
lines.script: [clipped, in charge] Girls, behind me. [low, slow, almost polite] You three have till I count to three. Then I'm getting the HOSE.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Three.
lines.script: [flat, immediate] [punchline] Three.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Nine papers. There were twelve. So the one with the pan still has three.
lines.script: [counting, small teacher] Nine papers. There were twelve. [working it out] So the one with the pan still has three.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Then it has three of my muffins and my pan. Keep walking.
lines.script: [grim, decided] Then it has three of my muffins and my pan. Keep walking.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: The grass is Boppy color!
lines.script: [delighted discovery] The grass is BOPPY color!

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: It's grey, Rose. Just that one spot. And that orange cube has a dragonfly in it.
lines.script: [correcting, patient] It's grey, Rose. Just that one spot. [curious, slower] And that orange cube has a dragonfly in it.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: He's stuck! Tata, get him out!
lines.script: [worried for him, loud] He's STUCK! [demanding] Tata, get him out!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Yes. Right away. Everybody give the dragonfly some room.
lines.script: [instant, serious, taking an order] Yes. Right away. [clearing the area] Everybody give the dragonfly some ROOM.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It's the size of a plum. I carried a suitcase through two airports this morning.
lines.script: [strained, out of breath] It's the size of a PLUM. [baffled at himself] I carried a suitcase through two airports this morning.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Your face is RED, Tata!
lines.script: [delighted] Your face is RED, Tata!

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata, stop. You're getting fingerprints on it. And look, it has a dent. Did you do that?
lines.script: [bossy] Tata, stop. You're getting fingerprints on it. [noticing] And look, it has a dent. [suspicious] Did YOU do that?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Grace. I couldn't even make it wobble.
lines.script: [flat, laughing at himself] Grace. [punchline] I couldn't even make it WOBBLE.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Deedee, what's that?
lines.script: [curious] Deedee, what's that?

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: A flashbulb, from an old camera. It's burnt. Somebody set it off right here and left it by your grandfather's chair.
lines.script: [plain, certain] A flashbulb, from an old camera. It's burnt. [annoyed] Somebody set it off right here and left it by your grandfather's chair.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Don't throw it out! It's a clue. I'm starting a new list. Burnt bulb. Grey grass. Orange cube with a dragonfly in it. I'm writing it in pencil.
lines.script: [alarmed] Don't throw it out! [important] It's a clue. I'm starting a new list. [writing, one at a time] Burnt bulb. Grey grass. Orange cube with a dragonfly in it. [firm] I'm writing it in PENCIL.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Why pencil?
lines.script: [curious, respectful] Why pencil?

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Because I don't know what any of it means yet.
lines.script: [honest, plain] Because I don't know what any of it MEANS yet.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: GAH! Grace, I'm holding your hand. That's for me, not for you.
lines.script: [real yelp] GAH! [quiet, amazed at himself] Grace, I'm holding your hand. [punchline, honest] That's for ME, not for you.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: I know, Tata. You're squeezing. Is that the Big One? Boppy only said it was as big as the couch!
lines.script: [small, scared] I know, Tata. You're squeezing. [loud question] Is that the Big One? Boppy only said it was as big as the COUCH!

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: For once in his life he rounded down.
lines.script: [dry, staring up at it] [punchline] For once in his life he rounded DOWN.

lines.speaker: The Big One
lines.text: GLUB. I was small at breakfast. Then a flash. Now I don't fit under my log.
lines.script: [huge, wet, slow] GLUB. I was small at breakfast. Then a flash. [glum] Now I don't fit under my log.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: And that's my good twelve-cup pan on your head. It's never been in pond water in its life.
lines.script: [sharp, pointing] And that's my good twelve-cup pan on your head. [offended, fast] It's never been in POND water in its life.

lines.speaker: The Big One
lines.text: It's my crown. A little muddy one brought it. I'm keeping it.
lines.script: [huge, stubborn] It's my crown. A little muddy one brought it. I'm keeping it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Mom. That's a boss. You don't just walk up to a boss.
lines.script: [urgent whisper] Mom. That's a BOSS. [earnest] You don't just walk UP to a boss.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: I worked the night shift, Tom. I've walked up to worse. Mister, take off my pan.
lines.script: [unbothered, brisk] I worked the night shift, Tom. I've walked up to worse. [firm, to the fish] Mister, take off my pan.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: BOO!
lines.script: [full volume] BOO!

lines.speaker: The Big One
lines.text: GLUB! HA! You got me! I see everybody. I never saw you!
lines.script: [startled, then roaring with laughter] GLUB! HA! You GOT me! [amazed] I see everybody. I never saw YOU!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Nobody does. She's gotten me in an empty room.
lines.script: [dry, weary, fond] Nobody does. [punchline, flat] She's gotten me in an EMPTY room.

lines.speaker: The Big One
lines.text: Take the pan. The sneaky one gets this. It's the only thing I've got.
lines.script: [huge, gentle] Take the pan. The sneaky one gets this. [plain, a little shy] It's the only thing I've got.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Thank you, fish! There's a bug on my money!
lines.script: [thrilled, polite] Thank you, fish! [shouting the news] There's a BUG on my money!

lines.speaker: The Big One
lines.text: The man in the folding chair. Will he be back?
lines.script: [huge, careful, hopeful] The man in the folding chair. Will he be back?

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: That's Boppy. He's here every single day.
lines.script: [surprised] That's Boppy. [plain] He's here every single day.

lines.speaker: The Big One
lines.text: Good. He was in the middle of a story. The one about the race.
lines.script: [relieved] Good. He was in the middle of a story. The one about the race.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: He's been in the middle of that one for fifty-one years.
lines.script: [dry, level] [punchline] He's been in the middle of that one for FIFTY-ONE years.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Boppy! Your fish is REAL! He's CAR size and he gave me money!
lines.script: [shouting, running] Boppy! Your fish is REAL! He's CAR size and he gave me money!

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: CAR size? Cozy Rosie, I told everybody a couch. Twenty years! I didn't want to brag!
lines.script: [sharp lift, stunned] CAR size? [warm, goofy, injured] Cozy Rosie, I told everybody a COUCH. Twenty years! [punchline, big] I didn't want to BRAG!

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Now that's real gold. Same as these. Look.
lines.script: [impressed, slow] Now that's real gold. [proud] Same as these. Look.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: You've got money in your TEETH!
lines.script: [amazed, loud] You've got money in your TEETH!

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Safest place there is. Gold is for keeping, Cozy Rosie. You put that where nobody's going to look.
lines.script: [certain, chatty] Safest place there is. [plain, a rule] Gold is for keeping, Cozy Rosie. [conspiring] You put that where nobody's going to LOOK.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Under Lamby! Nobody looks under Lamby!
lines.script: [instant, certain] Under Lamby! [stating a fact] NOBODY looks under Lamby!

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Good girl. Now. Your grandmother promised me the first muffin. Who's got my muffin?
lines.script: [pleased] Good girl. [turning to business] Now. Your grandmother promised me the first muffin. [looking around] Who's got my muffin?

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: The fish ate them, Boppy. The last three.
lines.script: [plain, reporting] The fish ate them, Boppy. The last three.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: The fish gets THREE?
lines.script: [hurt, baffled, louder than before] [punchline] The FISH gets THREE?

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Twelve more. Forty minutes. The first one's still yours.
lines.script: [brisk, not looking up] Twelve more. Forty minutes. [quieter, plain] The first one's still yours.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Girls, you heard that. Forty minutes. Somebody watch the clock.
lines.script: [gleeful, showman] Girls, you heard that. FORTY minutes. Somebody watch the clock.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata, you have a job. If you see anything grey in California, or an orange cube, you write it down and text me.
lines.script: [bossy, serious] Tata, you have a JOB. If you see anything grey in California, or an orange cube, you write it down and text me.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I have a job. Yes. Does the job come with a pencil?
lines.script: [honored, serious] I have a job. Yes. [hopeful] Does the job come with a pencil?

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: That's my second best one. Don't lose it.
lines.script: [reluctant, sideways] That's my second best one. [firm] Don't LOSE it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Second best. It's going in the pocket with the zipper.
lines.script: [touched, formal] Second best. [solemn promise] It's going in the pocket with the ZIPPER.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: One more ride, Tata! To the cab! Go the LONG way!
lines.script: [demanding, loud] One more ride, Tata! To the cab! Go the LONG way!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The long way. That's all the way around the Square. Twice.
lines.script: [agreeing at once, official] The long way. [working it out, pleased] That's all the way around the Square. [beat] TWICE.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: hey babe. safe flight. the smog over 2nd ave turned purple this morning. it'll probably blow over.
lines.script: [mellow, easy] hey babe. safe flight. [tossed off] the smog over 2nd ave turned purple this morning. [punchline, level, light touch] it'll probably blow over.
